why: Every full-size run so far trained at a peak rate of 3e-4, and the best stack is 0.0103 behind the Transformer on test (v17). On the test bed both models are best at a higher rate. Going from 3e-4 to the best rate, the stack gains 0.013 more than the Transformer (learning_rate_with_data, seed 20001), and on new contexts, where the gap is, its gain is almost twice the Transformer's (learning_rate_by_context.json). full_size_rate_pilot measures each model's best rate at full size; this pair trains the best stack and its Transformer at those rates, to decide whether the stack beats the Transformer at full size.

arms.stack: v17's recipe (l2048-know-st): v16's stack with forgetting slopes, 24,000 updates on windows of 512 bytes, then forked onto unbroken streams of windows of 2,048 bytes with 128 knowledge cells a head and a reach of 2,048 for the remaining 66,000 (36,263,956 parameters), at the stack's best full-size rate by full_size_rate_pilot
arms.transformer: v17's reference (tf2048): 24,000 updates on windows of 512 bytes, then windows of 2,048 bytes for the remaining 66,000 (34,752,000 parameters), at the Transformer's best full-size rate by full_size_rate_pilot

rate_rule: Each model trains at its best rate in full_size_rate_pilot if that rate beats the model's own 3e-4 there by at least 0.010; otherwise its v17 run at 3e-4 stands in (l2048-know-st or tf2048) and is not retrained. Both stages of a run use the same peak rate, with 1,000 warmup updates and one cosine over 90,000 updates.
measure: As v17. The stack is read as a stream over the full enwik8 test and validation splits, at the reach chosen on the first 1,000,000 validation bytes (its trained 2,048 or 8,192), with fast output synapses on all levels at 2^24 (taught) and without. The Transformer reads windows of 2,048 bytes, 2,032 of history before 16 scored, frozen. Pairs are compared piece by piece (experiments/compare_stream_scores.py) and split by context (experiments/gap_by_piece.py).
reading: The stack beats the Transformer at full size if its taught test score is below the Transformer's with the paired 95% interval of the gap below zero, and the same holds on validation. Otherwise recorded: the gap on test and validation against v17's 0.0103 and 0.0193. The better rates close part of the gap if the test gap shrinks by at least 0.003.
seen_before_recording: v17's full-size scores (l2048-know-st 1.11702 / 1.14963, tf2048 1.10669 / 1.13033). The test bed's learning_rate_with_data seed-20001 arms and learning_rate_by_context.json. full_size_rate_pilot has no finished run.

amendment.change: The rate rule is applied by a script as soon as full_size_rate_pilot's six scores exist, not at the next session. If the stack qualifies, its arm is queued at once on the first GPU and starts the same night; it needs about 16 hours and spans windows by pause and resume. If the Transformer qualifies, its arm is queued held and is released by the next loop session for the next window, so that a run that cannot start yet does not hold up the test-bed queue behind it. The rule, the arms, the measure and the reading are unchanged.
amendment.why: Starting the longer arm the night the pilot ends brings the pair's verdict a day earlier at no cost to the test bed: the stack's arm would otherwise take the first GPU for the whole of the next window instead.
amendment.seen_before_amendment: No arm of full_size_rate_pilot has finished. fs-st12 and fs-tf12 were at update 9,000 of 24,000 (trainer validation windows 1.6133 and 1.5669, not this study's measure).

amendment_2.change: The stack arm (fsp-st) was held by hand at 2026-11-22T21:37:19Z, before the rate rule queued it, so that full_size_lifted_ceiling_pilot runs first (two 24,000-update arms on the first GPU, about 100 minutes). A script applies that pilot's reading when its scores exist: the stack arm then trains plain at the rate this record's rule chose, or with the pool that lifts the ceiling at the lifted pilot's better rate, and is released. The Transformer arm, the measure and the reading are unchanged; the arm's code is v17l either way, and the lifted ceiling adds no parameters.
amendment_2.why: The pilot's stack saturates its membranes at higher rates (2.7% of its reads' entries and 2.0% of its cells' at the bound at 1.2e-3, up to 11.8% at the top level), so its best rate may be set by its membranes; the pair would otherwise spend about 16 GPU hours on a stack that the pool that lifts the ceiling may beat.
amendment_2.seen_before_amendment: The pilot's scores at 1.2e-3 and 6e-4 (see full_size_lifted_ceiling_pilot.json); no lifted run and no pair arm has trained.

result.verdict: Not beaten. Each model at its best full-size rate after 90,000 updates: the stack scores 1.11287 on test and 1.14726 on validation with fast output synapses at the reach of 8,192, the best spiking score so far (v18: 1.11615 and 1.14908); the Transformer scores 1.07899 and 1.10480 frozen. The stack is 0.0339 behind on test (95% interval 0.0328 to 0.0351) and 0.0425 behind on validation (0.0414 to 0.0436); against the Transformer with taught output synapses, 0.0357 and 0.0428. Both at 3e-4 (v17) the gaps were 0.0103 and 0.0193: the better rates widened the test gap by 0.0236 and did not close part of it.
result.reading: The best rate pays the Transformer and hardly the stack at full length. Paired with its run at 3e-4, the Transformer gains 0.0277 on test (0.0271 to 0.0283) and 0.0255 on validation from 1.2e-3; the stack gains 0.0042 (0.0036 to 0.0047) and 0.0024 from 6e-4. In the pilot of 24,000 updates the two gains were alike (full_size_rate_pilot: 0.0218 for the stack from 3e-4 to 6e-4, 0.0295 for the Transformer from 3e-4 to 1.2e-3), so with data the stack's gain from a higher rate fades and the Transformer's stays; the census on trained weights (unit_density_by_rate.json) finds the stack's code thin where its gain from the rate stops. By context, the stack is ahead wherever its stream offers a copy: on test 0.074 bits a byte ahead on near copies (16.6% of the bytes) and 0.411 ahead on copies that only its reach finds (4.2%); on validation 0.058 and 0.364. It is behind on new contexts: 0.0895 on test (0.0861 to 0.0930), 73.7% of the bytes and 1.95 times the whole gap, and 0.0997 on validation (1.80 times the gap). As in v17 and v18 the gap is knowledge, not memory. The split by place in the word is a least-squares fit over pieces of 256 bytes, and for this pair the shares of first, second and third letters and of spaces after a word rise and fall together from piece to piece, so their values are unstable and are not read; the fourth letter on, 31.7% of the bytes, is 0.084 behind on test (0.069 to 0.098). The reach chosen on the first validation million is 8,192 (1.17391 against 1.19049 at the trained 2,048). Without fast synapses the stack scores 1.11460 on test and 1.14686 on validation at that reach, so its fast output synapses gain 0.0017 on test and lose 0.0004 on validation; as trained (reach 2,048, no fast synapses) it scores 1.13021 and 1.16117. The stack trained as the plain stack at 6e-4 (v17l code, no pool that lifts the ceiling).
